verdict.summary: You can build a public OAuth connection that users in independent Notion workspaces can authorize. Marketplace listing is optional. You do not need Marketplace review to use the OAuth connection. Choose the Any workspace installation scope carefully because it cannot be changed later. Enterprise workspace owners can restrict which connections users may install.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours, mostly OAuth setup and permission testing (estimate)
verdict.waitTime: None for public OAuth use without a Marketplace listing. An optional Marketplace listing is reviewed.
verdict.mainGate: To create a connection, you need workspace-owner access on Free or Plus. On Business or Enterprise, an owner can allow members or groups to create connections.

recommendation.text: Create a public connection with the Any workspace installation scope. This lets users from independent Notion workspaces connect through OAuth. Marketplace listing is optional.

sources.quote: Use a public integration so users in any workspace can authorize your app through OAuth. You can also apply to list it on the Marketplace.
For a public integration, choose Any workspace when you create it.

scopeTiers.text: Read-only retrieval needs the read content capability. It has no capability review. Users must still choose the pages and databases they share.

sources.quote: Capabilities determine which operations a connection or token can perform, such as reading pages, updating databases, or adding comments.
A user can search for and select pages and databases to share with the connection from the page picker.
Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace . You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

All other plans 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)

essentials.text: Exchange authorization codes only on your server using HTTP Basic authentication. Keep tokens in encrypted storage. If using webhooks, verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature over raw request bytes.

sources.quote: OAuth token endpoints under /v1/oauth/* do not send CORS headers on purpose. OAuth code exchange requires a client secret and must run on a server.
Store tokens in environment variables or an encrypted secret manager.
Pass the raw request body exactly as it arrived (re-serialized JSON produces different bytes and fails verification)

state If the user was in the middle of an interaction or operation, then this parameter can be used to restore state after the user returns. It can also be used to prevent CSRF attacks.

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the temporary authorization code for an access token and refresh token.

sources.quote: Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .

The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET , like so:
CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET

curl --request POST \
 --url https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token \
 --header 'Authorization: Basic <encoded-value>' \
 --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 --header 'Notion-Version: <notion-version>' \
 --data '
{
 "grant_type": "authorization_code",
 "code": "<string>",
 "redirect_uri": "<string>"
}
'

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens
requests.curl:
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token \
  --header "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID:YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET' | base64)" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Notion-Version: 2026-03-11' \
  --data '{
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "code": "AUTH_CODE",
    "redirect_uri": "YOUR_REDIRECT_URI"
  }'

requests.text: Retrieve the identity associated with the connected token.

sources.quote: The access_token will be used to authenticate subsequent Notion REST API requests.

requests.label: Check the connection
requests.curl:
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.notion.com/v1/users/me \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' \
  --header 'Notion-Version: 2026-03-11' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json'

detail.text: Use a workspace where you can create a connection. On Free and Plus plans, only workspace owners can create connections. On Business and Enterprise plans, workspace owners can also allow members or groups to create them. Only full members and workspace owners can own a connection; guests and limited-access members cannot.

sources.quote: On Free and Plus plans, only workspace owners can create connections.
Only full members and workspace owners can be owners. Guests and members with limited access can't.

detail.text: Open Build → Connections and create a connection. Choose Any workspace as the installation scope. Do this carefully because the choice cannot change later.

sources.quote: Go to the Developer portal. In the Build section, select Connections. This is also where you create OAuth integrations limited to selected workspaces.
Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can’t be changed afterward.

detail.text: Add your controlled callback URL and choose read content first. Add insert content or update content only for approved product actions. Users will see these capabilities during authorization.

sources.quote: Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including:
Connection capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, etc.)
Notion presents a prompt describing the connection’s capabilities — what it will be able to do in the user’s workspace.

steps.title: Draft callback safeguards

detail.text: Use state tied to the initiating user session. Send the code to your server for exchange with client-secret Basic authentication. Encrypt the returned access and refresh tokens.

sources.quote: state If the user was in the middle of an interaction or operation, then this parameter can be used to restore state after the user returns.
OAuth code exchange requires a client secret and must run on a server.
Notion responds to the request with an access_token , refresh_token , and additional information.

detail.text: Store the client secret and each user's token record in encrypted server-side storage. Use separate development, staging, and production credentials. Never put the client secret in browser code.

sources.quote: Store tokens in environment variables or an encrypted secret manager.
Use separate tokens for development, staging, and production.

detail.text: Authorize in the development workspace. Test selected pages, denied access, parent-page sharing, and least-privilege capabilities. Confirm your agent cannot access unshared content.

sources.quote: A user can search for and select pages and databases to share with the connection from the page picker.
Selecting a parent page also grants access to its child pages.
Capabilities and content access work together: permission to update pages does not grant access to every page.

detail.text: Exercise refresh and authorization again. Replace both stored tokens as one database operation. Handle failed refreshes by asking the user to reconnect.

sources.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.
New public connections now mint a fresh access_token and refresh_token for each successful OAuth authorization

detail.text: Queue requests by workspace. Honor Retry-After on 429 and 529 responses. Use backoff and jitter because other connections can consume the same workspace budget.

sources.quote: Because it’s shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit.
Connections should handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After response header.

detail.text: Skip Marketplace listing for the first release. Your public connection can still use OAuth with any workspace. No provider review is required on this path.

sources.quote: Listing on the Marketplace is optional and helps your connection reach a wider audience, but your connection can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed.

detail.text: Only when you want Marketplace discovery, create listing metadata and assets in Listings → Connections. Submit only after the public connection is complete. This path requires provider review.

sources.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.
Save your listing as a draft. You can return to edit it at any time before submitting.

detail.text: When you submit an optional Marketplace listing, wait for Notion's email decision. Track its status in Listings → Connections.

sources.quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.
After submission, your listing moves to the Submitted section where you can track its review status.

detail.text: Send users to Notion's authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, and state. Use the same redirect URI in the code exchange when required.

sources.quote: The URL begins with https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and has the following parameters:
response_type Always use code . ✅
In most cases, the redirect_uri field is required.

detail.text: Only when you need event notifications, register a public HTTPS webhook endpoint. Verify X-Notion-Signature against the raw body before processing any event.

sources.quote: It must be a secure (SSL) and publicly available endpoint. Endpoints in localhost are not reachable.
Every webhook request from Notion includes an X-Notion-Signature header
Pass the raw request body exactly as it arrived (re-serialized JSON produces different bytes and fails verification)

gotchas.text: Choosing Any workspace is irreversible. This applies when creating the connection. Create a new connection if you later need selected-workspace access instead.

sources.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can’t be changed afterward.

gotchas.text: Capabilities do not grant all workspace content. This applies after every authorization. Users must share content in the page picker.

sources.quote: Capabilities and content access work together: permission to update pages does not grant access to every page.

gotchas.text: Refresh tokens rotate. This applies whenever you refresh or reauthorize. Replace access and refresh tokens together to avoid losing the current credential.

sources.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.
New public connections now mint a fresh access_token and refresh_token for each successful OAuth authorization

gotchas.text: Workspace request budgets are shared. This applies when customers have several Notion connections. Your agent can be throttled even below its own connection limit.

sources.quote: Because it’s shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit.

gotchas.text: Marketplace review is optional but required for Marketplace discovery. This applies only after you submit a listing. Public OAuth use does not need it.

sources.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace . You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

whenBlocked.text: If you cannot create a connection, ask the workspace owner to create it or delegate connection creation. This applies on Free and Plus workspaces without owner access.

sources.quote: On Free and Plus plans, only workspace owners can create connections.
On Business and Enterprise plans, workspace owners can also let members, or members in certain groups, create them.

whenBlocked.text: If a customer cannot install the connection, ask their workspace owner to allow it. This applies in Enterprise workspaces with restricted connections.

sources.quote: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members are allowed to install.
If a connection you're looking for isn't available, contact your workspace owner.

whenBlocked.text: If Marketplace changes are requested, update the listing and resubmit. This applies only after an optional listing review.

sources.quote: If changes are required, the Notion team sends feedback and you can resubmit after making updates.

detail: Notion documents four app/automation types: personal access tokens, internal connections, OAuth integrations, and public integrations. | quote: "Compare personal access tokens, internal connections, OAuth integrations, and public integrations for your Notion app or automation."

Personal access tokens are intended to automate the creator’s own work, using the creator’s Notion permissions. | quote: "Use a personal access token for scripts, tools, and Workers that run with your Notion permissions."

Internal connections are intended for shared workspace tools, with access granted independently of an individual user. | quote: "Use an internal connection for tools your team shares, with access granted to the connection independently of any one person."

OAuth integrations are for apps used in selected workspaces, with each user authorizing their own access. | quote: "Use an OAuth integration for internal tools where each person authorizes their own access."

Public integrations are for apps that users in any workspace can authorize through OAuth, and they may be listed on the Marketplace. | quote: "Use a public integration so users in any workspace can authorize your app through OAuth. You can also apply to list it on the Marketplace."

OAuth integrations and public integrations use the same OAuth authorization flow, but OAuth integrations are limited to selected workspaces while public integrations are available to any workspace. | quote: "OAuth integrations and public integrations use the same OAuth authorization flow. Here, OAuth integrations are limited to selected workspaces, while public integrations are available to any workspace."

Personal access tokens and internal connections have a one-workspace scope; OAuth integrations use workspaces selected when creating the integration; public integrations support any workspace. | quote: "Workspace scope One workspace. One workspace. Workspaces you select when creating the integration. Any workspace."

Personal access tokens use the creator’s access, internal connections use the connection’s own shared access, and OAuth/public integrations use each user’s separately authorized access. | quote: "Whose access does it use? Yours. The connection’s own access, shared by the tool. Each user’s separately authorized access. Each user’s separately authorized access."

Capabilities determine which operations a connection or token can perform, including reading pages, updating databases, and adding comments. | quote: "Capabilities determine which operations a connection or token can perform, such as reading pages, updating databases, or adding comments."

Capabilities do not by themselves provide access to every page; capabilities and content access work together. | quote: "Capabilities and content access work together: permission to update pages does not grant access to every page."

Personal access tokens use existing permissions without a separate sharing step, while internal connections require content access to be granted. | quote: "A personal access token uses your existing permissions. An internal connection needs content access granted to it."

For OAuth integrations and public integrations, users select pages during authorization; selecting a parent page also grants access to its child pages. | quote: "Each user selects pages in the OAuth page picker when authorizing the app. Selecting a parent page also grants access to its child pages."

Personal access tokens, internal connections, and OAuth integrations are not eligible for Marketplace listing; public integration listings are optional and subject to review. | quote: "Marketplace listing Not eligible. Not eligible. Not eligible. Optional, subject to review."

detail: OAuth authorization endpoint: `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize` | quote: "The URL begins with https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and has the following parameters:"
Authorization URL parameters include `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, and `owner=user`; `state` is optional. | quote: "response_type Always use code . ✅"

The `state` parameter can restore interaction state and help prevent CSRF attacks. | quote: "state If the user was in the middle of an interaction or operation, then this parameter can be used to restore state after the user returns."

No `scope` parameter is documented in the authorization parameter list; permissions are selected through Notion’s page picker. | quote: "A user can search for and select pages and databases to share with the connection from the page picker."

The configured redirect URI receives a temporary authorization code in the query string after the user grants access. | quote: "Notion generates a temporary code and sends a request to the redirect URI with the following information in the query string:"
The redirect query parameters are `code` and, when supplied, `state`. | quote: "code A temporary authorization code. ✅"

OAuth token endpoint: `POST https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token`; authorization-code exchange uses HTTP Basic Authentication with the client ID and secret. | quote: "Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token ."
The authorization-code token request uses `grant_type=authorization_code`, the temporary `code`, and conditionally `redirect_uri`. | quote: `"grant_type" string Always use "authorization_code" . ✅`

If `redirect_uri` was supplied in the authorization URL, or multiple redirect URIs are configured, it is required in the token request; otherwise it is not allowed. | quote: "If the redirect URI was supplied as a query param in the Authorization URL, this field is required."
The token response includes both an `access_token` and a `refresh_token`. | quote: "Notion responds to the request with an access_token , refresh_token , and additional information."
The page does not specify access-token or refresh-token lifetimes. | quote: "The access_token will be used to authenticate subsequent Notion REST API requests."

Refreshing uses the same token endpoint with HTTP Basic Authentication and `grant_type=refresh_token`. | quote: "Send the refresh_token provided from Step 4 as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token ."
Refresh-token requests contain `grant_type=refresh_token` and the returned `refresh_token`. | quote: `"refresh_token" string The "refresh_token" returned in the Authorization step. ✅"
Refreshing rotates both tokens: it generates a new access token and a new refresh token. | quote: "Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token."
PKCE is not described; the documented token exchange is authorized with client-secret-based HTTP Basic Authentication. | quote: "The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication."

Creating a connection requires a name and development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, and capabilities. | quote: "Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including:"

log.name: read
detail: The Notion API enforces both per-connection and per-workspace rate limits. | quote: "The Notion API enforces two rate limits: a per-connection limit and a per-workspace limit. Some endpoints also have their own limit."

Each connection’s request budget is calculated over a 60-second window according to the workspace plan. | quote: "Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace’s plan:"

Business and Enterprise workspaces have a per-connection limit of 600 requests per minute, averaging 10 requests per second. | quote: "Business and Enterprise 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second)"
All other plans have a per-connection limit of 180 requests per minute, averaging 3 requests per second. | quote: "All other plans 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)"

The per-connection budget may be used evenly or in a single burst within the 60-second window. | quote: "The budget can be spent at any pace within the window — spread out evenly or in a single burst."

When the per-connection limit is exceeded, Retry-After indicates the time until the window resets and is at most 60 seconds. | quote: "When a request exceeds this limit, the Retry-After value is the time until the window resets, so it is at most 60 seconds."

Data-source queries have a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection and return HTTP 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. | quote: "Querying a data source has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection. A request over this limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header."

A separate per-workspace limit is shared across all connections and can cause throttling even when each connection is within its own limit. | quote: "Because it’s shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit."
Retry-After for the shared workspace limit may exceed one minute. | quote: "Retry-After for this limit can be longer than a minute."
Requests exceeding a rate limit return the rate_limited error code and HTTP 429. | quote: "Requests that exceed a limit return a \"rate_limited\" error code and an HTTP 429 response."
The rate_limit_reason field identifies which rate limit was exceeded. | quote: "additional_data.rate_limit_reason says which limit was exceeded:"

A per-connection limit violation is identified by public_api_request_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_request_rate_limit This connection is sending requests too fast. Wait for Retry-After ."

A shared workspace-budget violation is identified by public_api_space_request_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_space_request_rate_limit The workspace’s shared budget is used up. Wait for Retry-After ."

Endpoint-specific throttling is identified by public_api_endpoint_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_endpoint_rate_limit This endpoint has its own limit. Wait for Retry-After ."

Connections should handle both HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After header. | quote: "Connections should handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After response header."

Retry-After is an integer number of seconds, and clients should use its returned value rather than a fixed delay. | quote: "The header value is an integer number of seconds. Use the returned value rather than assuming a fixed wait."

A 529 response means Notion is temporarily overloaded and should be retried like a 429. | quote: "A 529 response carries the \"service_overload\" code and means Notion is temporarily overloaded; retry it the same way as a 429."

When Retry-After is present, the response body also provides the wait duration in additional_data.retry_after. | quote: "the body repeats the wait as additional_data.retry_after , a string of whole seconds"

For 429 or 529 responses, pause new requests for at least Retry-After seconds, retry the failed request, and use exponential backoff with jitter for subsequent failures. | quote: "If another 429 or 529 arrives, increase the delay with exponential backoff and jitter."

A 429 with public_api_request_blocked should not be retried because the connection’s API access is restricted. | quote: "Do not retry every error. Retry 429 and 529 responses, except a 429 with public_api_request_blocked ."

detail: The endpoint exchanges an authorization code for access and refresh tokens via `POST /v1/oauth/token`. | quote: `"summary":"Exchange an authorization code for an access and refresh token"`

Client authentication uses a required HTTP Basic Authorization header containing base64-encoded `username:password`. | quote: "Basic authentication header of the form Basic <encoded-value> , where <encoded-value> is the base64-encoded string username:password ."
The `Notion-Version` header is required; the latest API version shown is `2026-03-11`. | quote: "The API version to use for this request. The latest version is 2026-03-11 ."

For authorization-code exchange, `grant_type` and `code` are required, and `grant_type` must be `"authorization_code"`. | quote: `"required":["grant_type","code"],"properties":{"grant_type":{"type":"string","const":"authorization_code"`

The authorization-code request may include `redirect_uri` and `external_account`; `external_account` requires `key` and `name`. | quote: `"redirect_uri":{"type":"string","uniqueKey":"oneOf.0.redirect_uri"},"external_account":{"type":"object"`

For refresh, the request requires `grant_type: "refresh_token"` and a `refresh_token`. | quote: `"required":["grant_type","refresh_token"],"properties":{"grant_type":{"type":"string","const":"refresh_token"}`

For public connections, `redirect_uri` is required when it was included in the authorization URL or when multiple redirect URIs are configured. | quote: "The redirect_uri is a required field in the request body for this endpoint if:"
In most cases, the `redirect_uri` field is required. | quote: "In most cases, the redirect_uri field is required."

`redirect_uri` is disallowed when one redirect URI is configured and the authorization URL did not include the `redirect_uri` query parameter. | quote: "This field is not allowed in the request body if:"

A successful response requires `access_token`, bearer `token_type`, and `refresh_token` (which may be null), along with workspace and owner metadata. | quote: `"access_token" : "<string>" , "token_type" : "bearer" , "refresh_token" : "<string>" ,`

The page does not state access-token or refresh-token lifetimes, expiration durations, or refresh-token rotation behavior. | quote: "Creates an access token that a third-party service can use to authenticate with Notion."

log.name: read
detail: Notion’s credential-security guidance applies to OAuth access tokens. | quote: "This guidance applies to internal connection API tokens, OAuth access tokens, and personal access tokens."

Anyone obtaining a token can use its permitted capabilities and content permissions, potentially exposing or changing workspace content. | quote: "Anyone who obtains a token can make requests allowed by its capabilities and content permissions."

Tokens should be stored in environment variables or an encrypted secret manager rather than source code or configuration files. | quote: "Store tokens in environment variables or an encrypted secret manager."

OAuth integrations for other users should exchange the OAuth authorization code for a token on a controlled server. | quote: "For apps that other people use, create a public connection, which uses OAuth. Exchange the OAuth code for a token on a server you control."

Notion’s OAuth token endpoints intentionally omit CORS headers, and code exchange requires a client secret on a server. | quote: "OAuth token endpoints under /v1/oauth/* do not send CORS headers on purpose. OAuth code exchange requires a client secret and must run on a server."

Internal connection tokens and client secrets must not be exposed in browser page source because viewers could use them to act as the connection. | quote: "Never ship an internal connection token or a client secret in page source that strangers can load."

Secret scanning should block commits containing tokens and alert the token owner when a token is detected. | quote: "Enable secret scanning in your repository and CI system. Block commits that contain tokens, and alert the token owner if a token is detected."

Long-lived tokens should be replaced on a schedule and when someone with access leaves the team. | quote: "Replace long-lived tokens on a schedule and whenever someone with access to them leaves your team."
A potentially exposed token should be revoked or replaced immediately. | quote: "Revoke or replace a token immediately if it may have been exposed."

After token replacement, every application and environment using the old token must be updated, tested, and cleaned of the old value. | quote: "Replace the old token in every application and environment that used it. Test the new token, and remove the old value from configuration files and documentation."

log.name: read
detail: Webhook endpoints must be secure and publicly reachable; localhost is not supported. | quote: "It must be a secure (SSL) and publicly available endpoint. Endpoints in localhost are not reachable."

Subscription verification uses a one-time POST request containing a verification token. | quote: "When you create a subscription, Notion sends a one-time POST request to your webhook URL. The body of the request contains a verification_token"
The verification token proves Notion can reach the endpoint. | quote: "which proves that Notion can successfully reach your endpoint."

The verification token should be extracted from the incoming JSON payload and may be securely stored for later validation. | quote: "Inspect the incoming request at your endpoint and extract the verification_token from the JSON payload."
Payload signature validation is recommended for production but is optional. | quote: "While payload validation is optional, we recommend implementing it for any production environment."
Every webhook event includes an `X-Notion-Signature` header. | quote: "Every webhook request from Notion includes an X-Notion-Signature header"
The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the request body signed with the verification token. | quote: "which contains an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the request body, signed with your verification_token ."
The computed signature must match the received signature before trusting the payload. | quote: "If they match, the payload is trustworthy."

Signature verification must use the raw request body exactly as received; re-serializing JSON causes verification to fail. | quote: "Pass the raw request body exactly as it arrived (re-serialized JSON produces different bytes and fails verification)"

The JavaScript/TypeScript SDK helper performs constant-time comparison. | quote: "@notionhq/client v5.23.0 and later includes a verifyWebhookSignature() helper that performs this check for you, including the constant-time comparison."

Signature verification requires the raw body, signature header value, and verification token. | quote: "Pass the raw request body exactly as it arrived, the X-Notion-Signature header value, and your verification_token"

If a webhook subscription is rotated or recreated, the stored verification token must be updated. | quote: "If you ever rotate or recreate your webhook subscription, be sure to update your stored verification_token ."

detail: Notion MCP requires OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE, Streamable HTTP, token refresh handling, and secure credential storage. | quote: "Your client must support: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE Streamable HTTP ( /mcp ) Token refresh handling Secure credential storage"

The documented flow applies to Notion’s hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`, rather than establishing requirements for Notion’s standard REST API OAuth connection. | quote: "Notion provides a hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets MCP clients work with Notion workspaces."

PKCE is mandatory, and the client must verify that the authorization server advertises S256 support before authorization. | quote: "PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) is mandatory for secure OAuth flows."

The code verifier must remain secret until token exchange and must be stored securely. | quote: "The codeVerifier must be kept secret and never sent to the authorization server until the token exchange step."

Recommended verifier storage includes encrypted session storage, a secure cookie, or short-lived in-memory storage. | quote: "Store it securely (encrypted session, secure cookie, or in-memory with short expiry)."

The authorization request must include the protected resource URL as `resource`, binding the access token to Notion MCP. | quote: "Include the protected resource URL as resource in the authorization request and token exchange. This binds the access token to Notion MCP."

The authorization request must include `state`, `code_challenge`, and `code_challenge_method=S256`; the example also uses `redirect_uri`. | quote: "code_challenge: codeChallenge , code_challenge_method: \"S256\" , prompt: \"consent\""

State must be cryptographically random and stored with the code verifier in secure session storage. | quote: "const state = generateState() ... // Store state and codeVerifier in secure session storage"
The example generates state using 32 random bytes encoded as hexadecimal. | quote: "function generateState () : string { return randomBytes ( 32 ). toString ( \"hex\" ) }"
Production redirect URIs must use HTTPS; HTTP is permitted only for localhost development. | quote: "Always use HTTPS for redirect URIs in production"
Stored state and verifier values should expire after 10 minutes. | quote: "Set a short expiry (10 minutes) for stored values"
The callback must validate the returned `state` against the stored state to prevent CSRF. | quote: "Validate state on callback to prevent CSRF attacks"

The callback example rejects a callback whose `iss` does not equal the Notion MCP origin. | quote: "if ( params . iss !== mcpUrl . origin ) { throw new Error ( \"Unexpected authorization server\" ) }"
The callback must reject a missing or mismatched state value. | quote: "if ( params . state !== storedState ) { throw new Error ( \"Invalid state parameter - possible CSRF attack\" ) }"
The authorization code exchange must send the exact original `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`, client ID, and MCP resource URL. | quote: "code_verifier: codeVerifier , })"
Token exchange must be performed server-side for browser-based clients; the browser should only handle redirects. | quote: "Do token exchange server-side; browser should only handle redirects"

Tokens must be stored securely: web applications must keep them server-side and never in localStorage or cookies. | quote: "Web applications: Store tokens server-side only, never in localStorage or cookies"
Tokens must be encrypted at rest. | quote: "Always encrypt tokens at rest"

The page explicitly says an MCP access token is restricted to Notion MCP and must not be sent to the Notion REST API. | quote: "An MCP access token works only with Notion MCP. Don’t send it to the REST API"

Notion MCP’s OAuth flow requires discovery and validation of the resource metadata, issuer, authorization endpoint, and S256 support before redirecting. | quote: "Discover the OAuth issuer and endpoints before redirecting the user."

detail: `ntn workers create` creates a worker without deploying code and accepts `--name <name>`. | quote: "ntn workers create Create a worker without deploying any code. Flags: --name <name> ."

`ntn workers deploy` creates a worker when `workers.json` is missing, or updates the existing worker when it is present. | quote: "Creates a new worker if workers.json is missing; otherwise updates the existing worker."

`--workers-config-file <path>` specifies a workers manifest file, and its `workspaceId` selects the workspace for authenticated commands. | quote: "Path to a workers.json config file (overrides the default lookup in the current directory). The workspaceId field in this file selects the workspace"
Worker IDs can be supplied with `--worker-id` or obtained from the `workerId` field in `workers.json`. | quote: "The workerId field in workers.json in the current directory."

`ntn workers databases attach <database-key> <database>` binds a declared database to an existing Notion database using a database URL or data source ID. | quote: "Bind an attached database declaration to an existing Notion database. <database> is a database link/URL or a data source ID."

`ntn workers databases list [worker-id]` reports databases declared in the worker manifest, including whether each is managed or attached and whether it is bound. | quote: "List every database declared in the worker’s manifest, its lifecycle type ( managed / attached ), and whether it’s bound to a Notion database yet."
The CLI supports OAuth connections for capabilities that authenticate with external providers. | quote: "Manage OAuth connections for capabilities that authenticate against external providers."

`ntn workers oauth start <key>` starts an OAuth flow and opens the provider authorization URL. | quote: "ntn workers oauth start <key> Start an OAuth flow for an OAuth capability. Opens the provider’s authorization URL."

`ntn workers oauth show-redirect-url` prints the redirect URL to configure in the external provider or OAuth app. | quote: "ntn workers oauth show-redirect-url Print the OAuth redirect URL to configure with your provider."

`ntn workers oauth token <key>` prints an OAuth access token for debugging; `--plain` outputs only the token for piping. | quote: "Print an OAuth access token for a capability. Intended for debugging. With --plain , prints just the token for piping."
